name: Automation Startup Reservation Refinement
changes: Shortens crash-recovery treatment for unproven pending-* Automation handoff reservations to 120 seconds instead of allowing stale pending records to consume queue capacity for the full ten-minute startup recovery window.

Keeps the stronger ten-minute startup reconciliation window for recent persisted targets that have a durable non-pending collection identity, preserving v3.6.38 protection while SAB queue/history ownership is reconstructed after an unclean restart.
Removes the static max-grab allowance calculated from the first queue snapshot and lets the existing authoritative pre-Grab occupancy recheck govern admission throughout the cycle.

Makes the per-cycle search budget depend on configured queue depth rather than initially perceived free slots, so capacity that becomes available while a cycle is running can be used without waiting for another long retry interval.
Preserves the v3.6.38 recovered-import reconciliation, sole recovered paused-job repair, engine-ready gate, Smart Import protections, and non-destructive queue behavior.
regression_guards: pending-* or missing collection identities are never treated as durable recovered SAB jobs and expire from persisted startup capacity after at most 120 seconds.
Durable recovered collection identities still participate in the existing bounded ten-minute startup guard and 12-hour recency filter.
Every automatic Grab still performs an authoritative live occupancy recheck immediately before queue admission; this release does not weaken the v3.6.38 overfill protection.
Recovered completed-import reconciliation, no-downgrade behavior, release matching/blacklisting, manual Search/Grab, and Smart Import remain unchanged.
v3.6.37 activity feedback, v3.6.36 Automation action wiring, and v3.6.35 Manual Import live progress remain required production markers.
